column3: The Hebrew counts “seventy souls” coming from Jacob’s “thigh,” then separately states that Joseph was in Egypt; it does not say “including Joseph.”
The Hebrew includes the image “swarmed” and says “very, very mighty.”
The Hebrew compares them as “more numerous and mightier than we,” without explicitly saying “too.”
The Hebrew uses the collective singular “it” for the oppressed people and the builder of the cities.
The Hebrew calls the birthstools “the two stones.”
The Hebrew says He made “houses” for them where BSB explains “families of their own.”
“To the Hebrews” is supplied in BSB.
